name: Netlify
summary: Netlify hosts static sites and full-stack web apps with automatic deployments from Git and built-in serverless functions.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan gives 300 credits a month; bandwidth costs 20 credits per GB, so about 15GB total, enough for roughly 100 typical users.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Personal plan is $9/month for one developer and includes 1,000 credits a month, versus 300 on the Free plan.

portability.note: Site code is standard, but Netlify Functions, redirects, and Edge Functions use Netlify-specific config that needs rework to move.

runtime_model.note: Server-side code runs as Netlify Functions (AWS Lambda-based serverless) and Edge Functions, not a persistent server.

persistent_disk.note: Functions have no writable persistent filesystem between invocations; use Netlify Blobs or an external database instead.

long_lived_connections.note: Netlify Functions are short-lived and stateless, so they cannot keep a WebSocket connection open. Use a third-party realtime service.

background_workers.note: Background Functions run per invocation for up to 15 minutes; there is no always-on worker process separate from requests.

scheduled_jobs.note: Scheduled Functions run on a cron expression natively, with no extra service needed.

free_plan_commercial_use.note: Netlify's policy allows charging your own customers on the Free plan; you just cannot resell Netlify's hosting itself.

framework_support.note: Next.js runs with full SSR, ISR, and image optimization via Netlify's OpenNext adapter; static Vite apps and SvelteKit (adapter-netlify) are both fully supported. Express runs only inside a Netlify Function through the serverless-http adapter, with function time and memory limits. Go runs only as Lambda-compatible functions, not as a normal net/http server. Functions are written in JavaScript, TypeScript or Go, so Python, Ruby, PHP, Java and .NET apps cannot run.

custom_domain_free.note: Netlify's free plan includes custom domains with free managed SSL at no extra cost.

free_plan_sleeps.note: Netlify serves sites from a CDN and runs functions per request rather than an always-on server, so a free site never needs to wake up after inactivity.

bandwidth_included.value: Free: about 15 GB a month (300 credits at 20 credits per GB). Personal ($9/month): about 50 GB (1,000 credits), plus optional extra credits.
bandwidth_included.note: Netlify bills bandwidth in credits rather than GB directly, and once a free site's monthly credits run out Netlify pauses it until the next cycle.

setup.step: Sign up at netlify.com and click Add new project > Import an existing project.
Connect your Git provider and choose the repository to deploy.
Confirm the build command and publish directory; Netlify auto-detects most frameworks.
Add environment variables under Site configuration > Environment variables, then deploy.

builder_notes: Free plan is capped at 300 credits a month, about 15GB of bandwidth; a single popular post can exhaust it and pause the whole site.
Functions cannot hold WebSocket connections open; use a third-party realtime service for chat or live updates.
Background Functions cap out at 15 minutes and are not an always-on worker; use an external queue or worker service for long jobs.
